about.title: Los Alamitos Workplace Injury Claims
about.longDescription: Los Alamitos may be a small city, but its mix of industrial parks, retail corridors along Katella Avenue and Los Alamitos Boulevard, and proximity to I-605 means workers here face real on-the-job risks — from warehouse falls to delivery-vehicle collisions. Under California law, workers' compensation is typically your only path against your employer, no matter who was at fault. But if a subcontractor, property owner, equipment manufacturer, or another driver contributed to your injury, you may have a separate claim outside the workers' comp system. Sorting out which path applies — or whether both apply — takes a careful look at how the injury happened. LawProactive doesn't practice law or handle claims directly; we simply connect injured workers in Los Alamitos with an independent attorney who can review the facts and explain the options, at no upfront cost to you.

whyChoose.title: Why Talk to an Independent Attorney First

items.title: Workers' Comp Isn't Always the Whole Story
items.desc: California treats workers' comp as the usual exclusive remedy against your employer, but a negligent third party — like a subcontractor or equipment maker — can still be separately liable. An attorney can help identify whether that applies to your situation.

items.title: Reporting Deadlines Matter
items.desc: California law generally requires reporting a workplace injury to your employer within 30 days. Missing that window can complicate your claim, so early guidance matters.

items.title: Retaliation Is Illegal, But Workers Still Worry
items.desc: It's against California law for an employer to retaliate against you for reporting an injury or filing a claim. An independent attorney can help you understand your protections if you're concerned about your job.

items.question: I was hurt on a job site near Katella Avenue by equipment owned by another company. Do I have options beyond workers' comp?
items.answer: Possibly. If a third party — such as an equipment supplier or subcontractor — was negligent, California law allows a separate injury claim outside the workers' comp system. An independent attorney can review the details and let you know if this applies. Third-party claims generally carry a 2-year deadline, so it's worth exploring sooner rather than later.

items.question: How long do I have to report my injury to my employer in Los Alamitos?
items.answer: California law generally calls for reporting a workplace injury to your employer within 30 days. Waiting longer can create complications with your claim. If you're unsure whether you missed this window, an attorney can help you understand your next steps.

items.question: Can my employer fire me for filing a workers' comp claim?
items.answer: No — retaliation for reporting a workplace injury or filing a claim is illegal under California law. If you believe you've faced retaliation, an independent attorney can help you understand your rights and options. LawProactive can connect you with someone who handles these situations.
